affiliation_match.actual: Missing affiliations for: This study examined the role of social media in the spread, countering of cyber-extremism from an Islamic jurisprudential, educational perspective among students at Zayed University in the United Arab Emirates. A descriptive quantitative design was employed using a 28-item questionnaire administered to 180 students. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation analysis., The findings showed that X (formerly Twitter), TikTok, Instagram were the most frequently used social media platforms. Social media was perceived to play a moderate role in the spread of cyber-extremism, a stronger role in countering extremist ideologies through awareness, the promotion of balanced values. No statistically significant differences were found according to gender or duration of social media use, whereas significant age-related differences emerged regarding perceptions of social media's role in countering cyber-extremism. A weak but statistically significant negative correlation was also found between the two study dimensions. The study highlights the importance of integrating Islamic jurisprudential principles, educational approaches to promote moderation, responsible digital engagement, resilience against cyber-extremism. It recommends strengthening digital citizenship initiatives, educational programs that reinforce balanced Islamic values among university students.
